text: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ and brother of James, to those who are called, loved in God the Father and kept for Jesus Christ:
May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.
Beloved, while I was eager to write to you about the salvation we share, I found it necessary to write and urge you to contend for the faith that was once for all entrusted to the saints.

For certain people have slipped in among you—people long ago marked out for this condemnation—godless men who twist the grace of our God into a license for sensuality and who deny our only Master and Lord, Jesus Christ.
Now I want to remind you, though you already know it all, that Jesus, having once saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe;

versions.text: Now I want to remind you, though you know it all already, that the Lord, having once saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who did not believe;
versions.explanation: The base Greek text printed here reads Ἰησοῦς ("Jesus"), not κύριος ("the Lord"). The translation should follow the text it is based on, with a footnote noting that some manuscripts read "the Lord" (e.g., "Some manuscripts read 'the Lord'"). Also, 'though you know it all already' reads more smoothly as 'though you already know it all'.

text: and the angels who did not keep to their own domain but abandoned their proper dwelling he has kept in eternal chains under darkness for the judgment of the great day.

So also Sodom and Gomorrah and the surrounding cities, which in the same way indulged in sexual immorality and pursued unnatural desire, stand as an example, undergoing the punishment of eternal fire.
Yet in the very same way these men, carried along by their dreams, defile the flesh, reject authority, and slander the glorious ones.
But when Michael the archangel disputed with the devil about the body of Moses, he did not dare to bring a slanderous accusation against him, but said, "The Lord rebuke you!"
These people, however, slander what they do not understand, and by what they know only by instinct, like unreasoning animals, they are destroyed.
Woe to them! For they have taken the way of Cain, they have thrown themselves into Balaam's error for profit, and they have perished in Korah's rebellion.

These are hidden reefs at your love feasts, feasting with you while they shepherd only themselves without fear; waterless clouds driven along by the winds; barren trees in late autumn, twice dead, torn up by the roots;

versions.text: These are hidden reefs at your love feasts, feasting with you shamelessly, shepherds who care only for themselves; waterless clouds driven along by the winds; barren trees in late autumn, twice dead, torn up by the roots;
versions.explanation: The adverb ἀφόβως ("without fear") modifies the shepherding image, not the feasting. The current rendering shifts it to the previous clause and drops the shepherd metaphor's force; restoring it keeps the Greek structure while still reading naturally aloud.

text: wild waves of the sea, foaming up their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the gloom of darkness has been reserved forever.
It was also about these that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied when he said: "Look, the Lord is coming with tens of thousands of his holy ones,

versions.text: It was also about these that Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied when he said: "Look, the Lord is coming with his holy myriads,
versions.explanation: "Myriads" is an obscure loanword for oral reading; "tens of thousands of his holy ones" conveys ἁγίαις μυριάσιν more clearly and flows better when read aloud. (A footnote could note the Greek's prophetic past tense, literally 'the Lord came'.)

text: to execute judgment on all and to convict every godless person of all the ungodly deeds they have committed and of all the harsh words that godless sinners have spoken against him."
These are grumblers and malcontents, following their own desires; their mouths spew arrogant words, and they flatter people to gain advantage.
But you, beloved, remember the words spoken beforehand by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.
They told you that in the last time there would be scoffers, following their own godless desires.
These are the ones who create divisions—worldly people, devoid of the Spirit.
But you, beloved, build yourselves up on your most holy faith, pray in the Holy Spirit,
and keep yourselves in the love of God as you wait for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ that leads to eternal life.
Have mercy on those who doubt;
save others by snatching them from the fire; and to still others show mercy mixed with fear, hating even the garment stained by the flesh.
Now to him who is able to keep you from stumbling and to present you before his glory without blemish and with great joy—
to the only God, our Savior, through Jesus Christ our Lord, be glory, majesty, power, and authority, before all time, now, and forever. Amen.
